name: Bavarian Cream
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: ½ oz. of gelatine or isinglass

ingredients.name: 2 teaspoonfuls vanilla or bitter almond extract

instructions.text: Soak the gelatine in just enough cold water to cover it, for an hour
Drain, and stir into a pint of the cream made boiling hot
Beat the yolks smooth with the sugar, and add the boiling mixture, beaten in a little at a time
Heat until it begins to thicken, but do not actually boil
Remove it from the fire, flavor, and while it is still hot stir in the other pint of cream, whipped or churned in a syllabub churn to a stiff froth
Beat in this whip, a spoonful at a time, into the custard until it is the consistency of sponge-cake batter
Dip a mould in cold water, pour in the mixture, and set on the ice to form

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Soak the gelatine in just enough cold water to cover it, for an hour
2. Drain, and stir into a pint of the cream made boiling hot
3. Beat the yolks smooth with the sugar, and add the boiling mixture, beaten in a little at a time
4. Heat until it begins to thicken, but do not actually boil
5. Remove it from the fire, flavor, and while it is still hot stir in the other pint of cream, whipped or churned in a syllabub churn to a stiff froth
6. Beat in this whip, a spoonful at a time, into the custard until it is the consistency of sponge-cake batter
7. Dip a mould in cold water, pour in the mixture, and set on the ice to form
